title.narrative: ILO Socio-economic integration of migrants from Venezuela
ILO Socioekonomisk integration av migranter från Venezuela

description.narrative: Stöd till ILO för genomförande av ett projekt för att stärka socio-ekonomisk integration av venezolanska migranter och flyktingar genom ökad tillgång till anständiga jobb i värdländerna.

Support to the ILO for a project aiming for socio-economic integration of migrants and refugees from Venezuela through increased access to decent jobs in their host countries.
The ILO project Providing Venezuelan migrants and refugees with access to decent jobs in their host countries contributes to the Swedish Regional Strategy for Development Cooperation in Latin America 2021-2025, in particular to its objective “to improve conditions for productive employment and decent work, in particular for migrants, refugees and internally displaced persons".This project seeks to provide opportunities for socio-economic development for migrants from Venezuela, as well as for host countries and communities. This collaboration is guided by the Regional Platform for Inter-agency Coordination “Response for Venezuelans” (R4V), where the ILO co-leads, jointly with the IOM, the Integration Sector of the Regional Platform.The project’s objective is to improve and increase levels of socio-economic integration of Venezuelan migrants and refugees in their host countries through a decent work approach.The project will be implemented from January 2022 - December 2024. It will cover four countries in the region: Colombia; Peru; Argentina and Dominican Republic. These countries have been selected based on the fact that they recently have implemented, or currently are implementing broad regularization efforts. The project thus builds on the possibilities created for migrants who have achieved a legal status allowing them to reside and work in their host communities, setting the ground for successful socio-economic integration. In this way the project has the potential to highlight how migrants can contribute to local and national development throughout the region and point to lessons learned and inspiring examples for other countries to increase regularization and strengthen integration. The project will start with a three months inception phase during which ILO will develop a detailed plan of implementation, a final detailed budget, a finalised log-frame and a monitoring framework. These documents together with the inception report presented at the end of the inception phase will be subject to Sida's approval.The project will include cooperation with a series of national and regional partner organisations and platforms such as South-American Conference on Migration, the Quito process, MERCOSUR, Community of Andean Nations, Ministries of Labour and Foreign Affairs, trade unions, public employment services and others.

The overall objective of the project is that the socio-economic integration of migrants and refugees in their host countries and communities has been improved through a decent work approach.
This will be developed through 4 outcomes:
1. Improved capacity of vocational training institutes to serve national (host) and displaced populations.
2. Increased decent employment opportunities for Venezuelan migrants and refugees and their host communities by strengthening the link between public employment services and the job market.
3. Enhanced labour opportunities for Venezuelan women migrants and refugees.
4. Strengthened labour market information and labour migration data systems.

title.narrative: Grant agreement contribution to ILO Lazos

description.narrative:
Implementation model:
Project Lazos was implemented with a multi-level intervention model that was positively validated by the external evaluation. The model operated at three complementary levels: Macro level: strengthening regional frameworks, consultative processes, and regional integration mechanisms related to migration and labor inclusion. Meso level: enhancing the capacity of key institutions, including public employment services and vocational training institutions, while also building the institutional capacities of strategic partners such as the private sector, trade unions, and diaspora organizations. Micro level: generating direct benefits for refugees and migrants through improved public services designed with a more inclusive approach.
Examples of key results:
Outcome 1. Strengthened Vocational Training Institutions The project contributed to institutional and regulatory advances in the Dominican Republic and Colombia, strengthening the capacity of vocational training institutions to support the labor market integration of refugees, migrants, and other vulnerable populations.
The project did not create any separate services for migrants, but supported adaptation of existing public and private services through adjustments that incorporate migrant and gender-responsive approaches. This reduced institutional resistance, strengthened service providers capacities, and enhances the long-term sustainability of project outcomes.
In the Dominican Republic the vocational training institution, INFOTEP, adopted an institutional policy and a specific protocol to facilitate access for Venezuelan refugees and migrants to vocational training programs and skills certification services. More than 4,000 Venezuelan nationals accessed INFOTEPs regular training offer between 2023 and 2024.
In Colombia the vocational training institution, SENA, institutionalized and implemented the Your-talent-is-recognized-strategy, designed to promote skills certification within the private sector. During its first phase, the initiative reached more than 1,000 companies and 118 SENA centers nationwide. SENA also institutionalized a tool-box for inclusive strengthening of soft skills through 15 workshops, thereby supporting the training of 54 career counselors and 373 job seekers. A guide for self-implementation of the workshops was developed to ensure the long-term sustainability of institutional capacities.
In partnership with UN Women, and under SENAs leadership, the project provided technical assistance for Womens' Certification Campaigns. A public and free initiatives implemented at national level in Colombia aimed at recognizing workplace skills, including those of women on the move. It reached more than 15 000 women of which about 1 500 has obtained certification, among them about 15 % migrant women.
Outcome 2: Increased Employment Opportunities and Strengthened Public Employment Services and Skills Certification
In Colombia a comprehensive redesign of the Public Employment Service web platform was carried out in a participatory way with inputs from users. The new design has incorporated a migrant-inclusive approach and also acsesibility techniques such as sign language interpretation. This has significantly improved the user experience and access to employment-related services.
In Argentina, the project enhanced territorial coordination and social dialogue through the establishment of multi-stakeholder local working groups in eight cities, helping to strengthen collaboration among key actors and improving the capacities of more than 400 public officials engaged in local employment opportunities and socio-economic integration of migrants.
The project supported the creation of the first Inter-Union Network on Labor Migration in Latin America and the Caribbean, that brought together and trained more than 300 trade union representatives to promote dialogue and action on labor migration issues.
At regional level the project consolidated the fair recruitment approach with a migrant-inclusive perspective through an updated training offer that incorporated both gender-sensitive and user-centered methodologies. This training initiative reached and strengthened the capacities for fair recruitment of more than 200 key stakeholders across the four countries where the project was implemented.
More than 20 guides for employment orientation were launched to overcome knowledge gaps and bureaucratic obstacles hindering the employment of migrants. The guides were segmented by user profile (local governments, Public Employment Services, employers, trade unions, and migrants).
Outcome 3 Improved capacities and conditions for the employability and entrepreneurship of migrant women
Four analyses of barriers to the socioeconomic integration of Venezuelan migrant women were conducted, one for each prioritized country. The findings were used as inputs for technical proposals aimed at adapting public services, training of key stakeholders, and support to advocacy efforts.
Targeted gender-focused pilot initiatives for employability were successfully implemented in Argentina and Colombia. In Argentina the private sector had a leading role in the development of a pilot that promoted labor market inclusion of highly qualified migrant women in the mining, oil, and gas sectors.
In Colombia employability services for women survivors of gender based violence were strengthened through the validation of a labor inclusion model based on employment profiling and individualized development plans with coordinated employability services (basic education, job interview preparation, technical training, and soft skills development) The initiative also included guidance for companies on reducing hiring biases and accessing tax incentives.
To strengthen migrant women's entrepreneurship the project introduced the ILO's global program Start and Improve Your Business in the four countries. The training methodology on business development services for sustainable enterprises was complemented with a gender-responsive guidance toolkit and was transferred to 16 institutions in the four countries providing entrepreneurship training. 198 facilitators were trained and 103 were certified and the entrepreneurship training reached 958 entrepreneurs of which 81% women and 50% migrants.
Outcome 4 Strengthened Regional Frameworks and Technical Cooperation
The Project implemented an advocacy strategy for regional and subregional platforms and mechanisms to incorporate or strengthen the objective of socioeconomic integration in their agendas. The strategy included partnerships and direct technical assistance to the technical secretariats and rotating presidencies of regional consultative processes and integration mechanisms as well as the provision of specialized technical inputs, in coordination with other United Nations agencies, funds, and programs.This enabled the reposition socioeconomic integration as a structural component of the regional response to migration and supported mechanisms to incorporate technical content related to employment, mutual recognition of skills, and institutional strengthening.
As a result, nine of the 17 platforms identified by the project incorporated or strengthened the objective of socioeconomic integration within their frameworks, representing 56% of the total relevant platforms identified in the region.
Among the most significant advocacy interventions is the technical assistance to the Pro Tempore Presidencies of the Quito Process. The technical and financial support from the ILO and the project team led to the update of the the Regional Socioeconomic Integration Strategy (ERISE) approved by the plenary session of the Quito Process in November 2025.
Among the concrete results of the technical cooperation is the creation of the Skills Passport, a regional mechanism for the mutual recognition of labor competency certification involving 15 countries in the region. The skills passport enables recognition of the competencies and skills of people on the move in host countries and enhance their access to formal employment. Based on a digital platform, the Skills Passport permits portability of labor competencies for people on the move. This facilitates recruitment and hiring processes, provides greater certainty to employers and ensures the quality of competency assessment processes.
In consultations with IOM and other stakeholders the project developed a toolkit to strengthen local government capacities for the socioeconomic integration of migrants and refugees in Latin America. It includes five modules containing practical tools on topics such as employment, entrepreneurship, productive ecosystems and integration policies.
The Toolkit is an important contribution to strengthening the localization approach to socio-economic integration of migrants as a relevant operational mechanism in a context characterized by declining development financing and weakening people-centered migration governance.
The Toolkit also provides a cost-efficient self-assessment that enables municipalities to identify gaps in their local integration responses and use the resources offered through the modules to address them.
The Lazos Project, in partnership with IOM, OAS, and UNHCR, has co-organized and continuously supported the Regional Meetings of Women Leaders of Diaspora Communities in Latin America and the Caribbean since 2023. The initiative has promoted capacity-building in leadership, advocacy and gender sensitive approaches to socioeconomic integration of migrants. It also helped increase the visibility of migrant and refugee womens contributions to socioeconomic integration across the region. On average, each meeting brought together 30 women leaders from 12 countries to work together on issues such as combating xenophobia, preventing human trafficking and addressing gender-based violence.
